jobs.occupation: Laboratory Technician at NIVI Research Center
jobs.description:
The research group of Associate Professor Stephan Brouwer is looking for an engaged laboratory technician with experience in molecular biology, immunology, mammalian cell culture, and preferably with experience in BSL2/GMO-2 practices and research. The position is permanent and open for appointment from 1 March 2027.

  About us
 The Novo Nordisk Foundation Initiative for Vaccines and Immunity (NIVI), launched in December 2023, has a unique mission to harness airway immunity through innovative vaccine research and development to prevent airborne epidemics. NIVI has two parts:

  · NIVI Research Center (NIVI-R): A state-of-the-art research center anchored to the University of Copenhagen, Department of Immunology and Microbiology (www.isim.ku.dk).

  · NIVI Development (NIVI-D): A company that focuses on translational sciences and advancing vaccine development.

  NIVI-R conducts scientific research, while NIVI-D works to quickly turn that research into new vaccine candidates. NIVI-D accelerates clinical trials (phases 1 and 2) and ensures a smooth transition to partners for later stages of development.

  By connecting science, innovation, clinical trials, regulatory processes, and product development, NIVI aims to streamline the journey from research to real-world vaccines.

  Your tasks
 As part of a newly established research center, you will contribute to the setup and development of a completely new laboratory. This will include assisting with laboratory organization, implementation of workflows and procedures, inventory management systems, and establishing best practices for laboratory operations. You will work closely with the other laboratory technicians and scientific staff within NIVI-R to create a well-functioning research environment while helping to ensure the smooth day-to-day operation of the laboratory.

  As the laboratory technician, you will carry out several routine laboratory tasks; including maintenance of mammalian cell lines, molecular biology protocols (e.g., Protein purification, IVT-mRNA synthesis, DNA and RNA extraction/purification, Western-Blot/SDS-PAGE, PCR, qRT-PCR), Immunological assays (e.g. ELISA/Luminex, Neutralization assay, Flow cytometry), preparation of laboratory reagents, and other daily lab routines.

  You will also participate in various research projects that involve the development of vaccines and the characterization of vaccine responses, and close collaboration with the group’s scientists.

  The following will also be part of the role:

   	
• Documenting all laboratory work accurately using electronic lab notebooks. 	
• Monitoring laboratory stocks and ensuring timely replenishment. 	
• Organizing the laboratory and related space to be a clean, safe, and functional environment.   Profile
 Essential experience and skills:

  We are looking for someone with experience in molecular biology techniques (e.g., PCR, western blot, DNA/RNA work), mammalian cell culture (e.g., maintaining, freezing, and characterizing cell lines), and immunologic assays (ELISA, Flowcytometry).

   	
• A degree as a laboratory technician (Academy Profession degree or similar) is required. 	
• You must be good at working independently and organized, and be self-motivated 	
• Have good interpersonal and communication skills, both in Danish and English; spoken and written   Desirable experience and skills:

   	
• Experience with laboratory research in (BSL-2/GMO-2) labs. 	
• Experience with immunological assays: Proficiency in techniques such as ELISA/Luminex, Western Blotting, or Flow Cytometry (FACS) to support vaccine efficacy studies. 	
• Experience with cell culture, routine mycoplasma testing, and the validation of sterile reagents and media. 	
• Experience in animal research (active FELSA/ABD certification).   Terms of salary and employment
 Your employment will be at NIVI Research Center, Department of Immunology and Microbiology, University of Copenhagen. The position is full-time (37 hours per week), permanent, and is open for appointment from 1 March 2027.

  Employment as laboratory technician will be in accordance with the agreement between the Danish Ministry of Finance and OAO/HK STAT. The position is placed in salary group 4.

  Depending on qualifications a supplement may be negotiated.

  Question
 For further information please contact Stephan Brouwer: stephan.brouwer@sund.ku.dk

  Application
 Please submit your application in English by clicking "Apply for position" below. 

  The application should consist of the following:

   	
• Letter of application/motivation (max 1 page) 	
• Your CV incl. education, a list of laboratory skills/techniques, previous employments, language skills and other relevant skills 	
• Copy of relevant certificate/diploma   Deadline for application is 9 December 2027, 23.59 CET.
 We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

   

  University of Copenhagen wish to reflect the diversity of society and welcome applications from all qualified candidates regardless of age, disability, gender, nationality, race, religion or sexual orientation. Appointment will be based on merit alone

jobs.occupation: Postdoc in Cognitive Computational Neuroscience and Human Movement Perception
jobs.description:
The Department of Psychology invites applications for a postdoctoral position in Cognitive Computational Neuroscience and Human Movement Perception by 1 March 2027 or after agreement.

  The position is a fixed-term position for 30 months/2.5 years.
 
 Introduction
 The postdoc will be part of a project entitled "Mapping Experience of Action: Redefining Theories of Consciousness" funded by the Independent Research Fund Denmark. The project is headed by Professor Thor Grünbaum and Associate Professor in Cognitive Psychology Mark Schram Christensen Department of Psychology, University of Copenhagen.

  This interdisciplinary project develops a novel scientific approach to the study of consciousness by investigating conscious experiences of movement. Combining psychophysical experiments, computational modelling, and philosophical analysis, it examines how bodily and neural signals contribute to movement awareness. The project aims to advance our understanding of consciousness and critically evaluate leading neuroscientific theories of conscious experience.

  Applicants are asked to develop a short project description for the postdoc. It is critical that applicants are able to situate their project and research plan within the framework of the overall project. It is a requirement that applicants request from Associate Professor Mark Schram Christensen (markc@psy.ku.dk) the original project proposal prior to submitting the application.

  Candidates with various background may be considered for the position. Examples of relevant backgrounds are PhDs in cognitive (neuro)science, computational neuroscience, cognitive modelling, biomedical engineering, sports science with a focus on behavioural neuroscience, or similar. The candidates are expected to have strong skills in cognitive modelling, experimental design, data handling and data analysis documented in relevant scientific publications.

  The postdoc will be working in close collaboration with the other project members which has academic backgrounds in cognitive neuroscience and philosophy, and student assistants with background in Cognitive Data Science.  The position will be placed in the Cognition, Intention and Action research group, part of the Section for Cognition and Brain Sciences, Department of Psychology.  It is expected that the successful candidate will be present, part of the team, and take part in the activities in the Lab on a daily basis.
 
 Duties and Responsibilities
 The primary focus of the postdoctoral position will be on research within the main project. However, a certain amount of teaching obligations may be required. Additional tasks beyond research and teaching may also be considered, but to a limited extent. The university will determine the final scope of the various responsibilities, and the emphasis may vary over time.
 
 Qualification Requirements 
 Appointment as a postdoctoral researcher requires research qualifications at a level at least equivalent to those obtained through the satisfactory completion of a PhD programme within the relevant field.

  Strong skills in data handling and analysis are crucial, and experience with cognitive/computational modelling within human behavioural science or neuroscience is key to the content of the project. 

  You can find further information about the qualification requirements for postdoctoral positions here: Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities (In Danish only).

  You can also find further information about the postdoctoral position on our English webpage on career paths for early‑career researchers at the University of Copenhagen: Career at The University of Copenhagen.
 
 Strategy of the Faculty of the Social Sciences
 The Department of Psychology is part of the Faculty of the Social Sciences. The faculty is a successful academic community that strives to put knowledge into action by:

  Engaging partners in the co-creation of knowledge, learning and social change.

  Empowering our students to become reflective and responsible citizens who have the vision, the knowledge and the competences to change society for the better.

  Energising global, European and Danish communities of knowledge by innovating research methodologies and by research findings with impact.

  For more on the faculty’s strategy, please see: Strategy for the Faculty of Social Science.
 
 Assessment Criteria
 Applicants will primarily be assessed in relation to their research qualifications, including their publications, ability to conduct independent research and participate in research collaborations, and their experience of research management. In addition, the applicant’s research plan and research potential will be assessed in relation to the overall project described above.

  Teaching qualifications are not a requirement.
 
 Application
 Please submit your application online. To apply, please click on the “Apply now” icon at the bottom of this page. The application must be written in English, and include the following attachments in PDF or Word format:

   	
• CV (max. 3 pages) 	
• Cover letter including the preferred starting date (max. 1 page) 	
• Documentation of qualifications (exam certificates and PhD diploma) 	
• Complete publication list (attached publications must be marked with an asterisk). The list must be structured systematically and divided into the following categories: 	 		
• Peer-reviewed publications: 		
• Monographs and anthologies 		
• Articles in journals 		
• Book chapters/anthology contributions, etc. 		
• Non-peer-reviewed publications: 		
• Publications disseminating research findings, etc.
 		  	 	 	
• You can attach a maximum of 3 publications. The publication dates must be clearly marked on the list. The selected publications must be uploaded as attachments and numbered 1-3.
 	  	
• A short project description (max. 2 pages). 	 		
• The description should outline your ideas for the postdoc project situated in the state-of-the-art research in the field of the project. It should include your proposals for specific types of experimental and modelling approaches that you envision to contribute with to the project. The description must not exceed 2 standard pages, corresponding to approx. 4,800 characters (including title, punctuation, figures, footnotes and references, but excluding bibliography). A substantial breach of this will result in the application being excluded from consideration.
 		  	 	 	
• Research plan (max. 2 pages) 	 		
• The plan should include a brief account of previous research, current research projects, and a forward-looking outline of planned research contribution over the coming years. This may include specific references to the project proposals funded by Independent Research Foundation Denmark, and how the candidate expect to contribute to the project at large. 	 	   
 Salary and Terms of Employment
 Terms of appointment and salary will be in accordance with an agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC). The salary range for postdoctoral positions starts at DKK 39,000/approximately EUR 5,100 + an 18.07 % pension contribution. It is possible to negotiate salary supplements on an annual basis.
 
 Recruitment Process
 After the application deadline, the Head of Department will consider advice from the appointment committee and select applicants for assessment. All applicants will be notified whether they have been shortlisted. The Head of Department will set up an expert assessment committee to assess the shortlisted applications. The selected applicants will be informed who is serving on the committee. Each shortlisted applicant will be offered the opportunity to comment on the committee’s assessment before the appointment is announced.

  You can find further information on our recruitment process at: Recruitment process.
 
 International Applicant?
 The University of Copenhagen offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including support before and during your relocation and career counselling to expat partners. Please find more information about our services at: For international researchers at the University of Copenhagen.
 
 An Equal Opportunity Workplace
 The University of Copenhagen is committed in its pursuit of academic excellence to equality of opportunity and to creating an inclusive working environment and therefore encourages all qualified candidates to apply, regardless of personal background, gender, sexual orientation, age, disability, ethnicity etc. To learn more about our diverse workplace and our participation in the HRS4R HR Excellence in Research, please visit HR Excellence in Research.
 
 Contact Information
 For additional information about the position, please contact Associate Professor Mark Schram Christensen at email markc@psy.ku.dk or phone +45-3532 2448.

  For more Information about the recruitment process, please contact HR South at hr-soendre@adm.ku.dk. Please refer to ID number: 211-2675/26-2I

  The application deadline is 1 December 2026 at 23:59 CET.

  Any applications or additional material submitted after the deadline will not be considered. However, changes may be made to the submitted application right up until the deadline.

jobs.occupation: Postdoc in computational multimodal data integration for crop stress regulatory networks
jobs.description:
The Department of Plant and Environmental Sciences (PLEN) invites applications for a postdoctoral position in computational biology, focused on the integration of multimodal single-cell, epigenomic and literature-derived data into gene regulatory networks. The position is financed by the Novo Nordisk Foundation through the Ascending Investigator grant “Accelerating crop resilience with AI-enabled gene function prediction and stress regulatory networks” (NNF26OC0113093).

  The position is for 3 years. Start date is 1 March 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The project  Climate-driven heat and drought increasingly destabilise crop yields, yet the gene regulatory networks that govern stress responses in crops remain poorly resolved, because they have mostly been measured in whole organs. This programme will resolve them at the level of individual cell types and their cis-regulatory elements, in four major Nordic crops – rapeseed, potato, wheat and barley – under heat, drought and the two combined.

  The postdoc is the computational integrator of the grant: the person who turns the data the grant generates into regulatory networks. The single-cell RNA-seq and ATAC-seq data are generated by a PhD student and a technician on the group’s 10x Genomics platform; your job begins when the sequencing reads arrive. This is a purely computational position – no wet-lab work is involved. Concretely, you will:

   	
• Build the analysis backbone for the single-cell stress atlases: quality control, doublet and ambient-RNA handling, integration across four species, three stress conditions, three organs and three time points, and cell-type annotation using conserved markers – with pipelines the PhD students can run and extend. 	
• Integrate the modalities into gene regulatory networks. Infer transcription factor–target relationships by extending the group’s TEA-GCN method to single-cell data; identify cis-regulatory elements from accessible chromatin using known motifs, de novo motif discovery, convolutional neural networks and DNA language models; and link the two into TF–CRE–target triplets. Benchmark against SCENIC+, MAESTRO and related frameworks and adopt what works. 	
• Rank regulatory relationships by conservation across the four crops to obtain a high-confidence core, and develop the comparative methods this needs. 	
• Connect the networks to the rest of the grant’s work: to the group’s literature-derived knowledge graph and gene-function predictions, and to the open web platform through which the grant’s data, models and predictions are shared, so that regulators and targets can be prioritised for validation in rapeseed with traceable evidence. 	
• Co-supervise and train the PhD students and master’s students on the computational side, and help build the group’s single-cell and multi-omics analysis capacity.   Who are we looking for?  You hold a PhD in bioinformatics, computational biology, genomics, plant molecular biology or a related field, and you have analysed single-cell or other high-dimensional omics data independently. We are looking for a computational scientist who can take raw multimodal data through to a defensible biological claim, and who is comfortable working alongside the experimentalists who generate the data.

  Essential:

   	
• A PhD (or a thesis submitted by the start date) in a relevant field 	
• Documented experience with the analysis of single-cell RNA-seq and/or single-cell ATAC-seq data, or with comparable multimodal genomic data 	
• Strong programming proficiency in Python or R, and experience building reproducible analysis workflows (e.g. Snakemake/Nextflow, version control, containers) 	
• A publication record demonstrating independent scientific contribution 	
• Excellent written and spoken English   Advantageous:

   	
• Experience with gene regulatory network inference, motif analysis or cis-regulatory element prediction 	
• Experience with deep-learning models of regulatory sequence (CNNs, DNA language models) or with graph-based methods 	
• Experience with comparative or cross-species analysis of transcriptomic data 	
• Experience with plant abiotic stress biology or with crop species 	
• Experience co-supervising students   Our group and research – and what do we offer?  The Mutwil group at PLEN works at the interface of comparative and evolutionary plant biology and AI-driven biological discovery. We build large cross-species gene expression atlases, comparative co-expression networks and knowledge graphs, and we use machine learning and large language models to turn the plant literature and omics archives into testable hypotheses. The group comprises several PhD students, postdocs and master’s students, and maintains a portfolio of widely used community resources under the .plant.tools domain, including PlantConnectome, CoNekt, diurnal.plant.tools and evorepro.plant.tools.

  The postdoc will work closely with the two PhD students funded by the same grant (literature-derived knowledge graphs and gene-function prediction; single-cell stress experiments) and with collaborators Prof. Ryan Lister (University of Western Australia, multimodal single-cell genomics) and Prof. Zoran Nikoloski (University of Potsdam, regulatory network inference).

  The group is part of the Department of Plant and Environmental Sciences (PLEN), Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen. We are located on the Frederiksberg Campus in Copenhagen. We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in a dynamic and international research environment. Computational resources include a 196-thread/1 TB RAM workstation and guaranteed GPU access through LUMI and uCloud.

  Inquiries about the position can be made to Associate Professor Marek Mutwil, mutwil@plen.ku.dk.

  Terms of employment  The position is covered by the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff. Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. Negotiation for salary supplement is possible.

• Names and contact details of two or three references   The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

Afterwards an assessment committee will be appointed to evaluate the selected applications. The applicants will be notified of the composition of the committee and the final selection of a successful candidate will be made by the Head of Department, based on the recommendations of the assessment committee and the interview committee. The applicant will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

jobs.occupation: Postdoc in Single-Molecule and Single-Vesicle Imaging of Neurodegenerative Diseases
jobs.description:
Are you interested in understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying neurodegenerative diseases using cutting-edge fluorescence microscopy and single-vesicle imaging? Do you want to contribute to uncovering how protein aggregation and membrane interactions drive the development of Parkinson's disease? Then the Department of Chemistry at Aarhus University invites you to apply for a postdoctoral position within the ERC Starting Grant-funded project SPARTA.

We are seeking a highly motivated and ambitious postdoctoral researcher to join our research group at the Department of Chemistry, Aarhus University. The successful candidate will develop and apply advanced single-molecule and single-vesicle imaging approaches to investigate the dynamic interactions between α-synuclein oligomers and biological membranes, aiming to uncover fundamental mechanisms of neurodegeneration and contribute to the development of novel strategies for early disease detection.

This is a fixed-term 2-year position starting on 1 February 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

The successful candidate will join the ERC Starting Grant-funded project SPARTA, aiming to uncover the molecular mechanisms of α-synuclein aggregation and membrane interactions in Parkinson’s disease.

The position will primarily involve:

• Investigating α-synuclein aggregation and interactions with lipid membranes.
• Developing and applying advanced single-molecule and single-vesicle fluorescence microscopy.
• Exploring how membrane composition and properties influence protein aggregation and membrane disruption.
• Performing quantitative image analysis and computational data analysis.
• Developing novel single-vesicle assays for studying neurodegenerative disease mechanisms.
The research will be conducted in an interdisciplinary environment at the Department of Chemistry, Aarhus University, in collaboration with researchers in biophysics, molecular biology, and neuroscience.

Your profile
We are looking for a highly motivated and ambitious postdoctoral researcher with a strong background in experimental biophysics and quantitative fluorescence microscopy.

The ideal candidate should have:

• A PhD in nanoscience, biophysics, biochemistry, or a related field.
• Experience with single-molecule or single-vesicle fluorescence microscopy, preferably TIRF microscopy.
• Experience with lipid membranes, liposomes, or protein–membrane interactions.
• Strong skills in quantitative image analysis and data processing, preferably using Python.
• Experience in scientific publishing and communicating research findings.
• Ability to work independently and collaboratively in an interdisciplinary research environment.
• Excellent communication skills in English, both written and spoken.
• Experience with α-synuclein, protein aggregation, or neurodegenerative diseases is an advantage but not a requirement.
We value scientific curiosity, creativity, independence, and a collaborative mindset.

Who we are
The Department of Chemistry at Aarhus University offers an international and interdisciplinary research environment with state-of-the-art facilities and strong collaborations.

The successful candidate will join the research group led by Assistant Professor Mette Galsgaard Malle, focusing on single-molecule and single-vesicle imaging to understand molecular interactions and disease mechanisms.

All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self.

jobs.description:
The Department of Plant and Environmental Sciences (PLEN) invites applicants for two PhD fellowships in AI-driven discovery of plant metabolic pathways – doctoral candidates DC7 and DC8 of the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network Stripes&Stars. Both projects are part of the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network Stripes&Stars (Grant Agreement No. 101312557), funded by the European Union under Horizon Europe. Stripes&Stars trains ten doctoral candidates across eight European countries in modern breeding of ornamental and fruit crops, using flower and fruit colour – anthocyanins and other flavonoids in petunia, calibrachoa, poinsettia and bilberry – as its scientific showcase. The University of Copenhagen hosts the network’s two data-science doctoral candidates (DC7 and DC8), who together provide the computational backbone for predictive colour and specialised-metabolite engineering.

  Start dates: DC7 is expected to start 1 June 2027 (month 3 of the network) and DC8 1 January 2028 (month 10 of the network), or as soon as possible thereafter. Please state in your application which project you are applying for; you may apply for both.

  Project DC7: Knowledge graph construction for specialised metabolite pathways (Stripes&Stars WP4–5)  Flavonoids and anthocyanins colour petunia flowers and bilberry fruit, protect plants against UV light and stress, and attract pollinators – and roughly 20% of the carbon flux in plants passes through the flavonoid pathway. Yet knowledge of the enzymes, transporters and regulators that control which pigment accumulates where is scattered across tens of thousands of papers. This project will make that knowledge computable.  You will:

   	
• Use the PlantConnectome large-language-model pipeline to extract and interlink knowledge on enzymes, substrates, transporters, transcription factors, stresses and genetic modifications that regulate pigment and specialised-metabolite biosynthesis, from more than 70,000 publications, into the first comprehensive knowledge graph of plant specialised-metabolite pathways 	
• Extend the graph to environmental context – in particular how concurrent stresses (e.g. high light with heat or drought) reshape pigment and specialised-metabolite accumulation, and whether the regulators involved are shared across ornamental and fruit species 	
• Apply symbolic reasoning and link prediction (e.g. AnyBURL rule mining and graph neural networks) to infer missing pathway components and regulatory relationships, yielding testable hypotheses and engineering targets for the experimental partners 	
• Build an interactive, ChatGPT-like interface to the graph, so that consortium members and the wider community can retrieve complete, evidence-linked information on genes, enzymes, pathways and phenotypes 	
• Work closely with DC8 (network-based pathway prediction, also at UCPH) so that graph and expression evidence are integrated into one explainable framework   Secondments: TU Wien (Prof. Heidi Halbwirth, 3 months) to integrate graph predictions with enzyme characterisation and pigment pathway analysis, and Klemm + Sohn (Stuttgart, 2 months) to validate predicted targets in an applied breeding context. An interest in plant metabolism is essential; a formal background in it is not.

  Project DC8: Multi-omics co-expression networks for predicting novel metabolic pathways (Stripes&Stars WP4–5)  Which genes make a petunia petal purple, a poinsettia bract white, or a bilberry flesh blue? Many of the enzymes, transporters and regulators are still unknown, and the ones we know were found one at a time. This project will find them systematically from expression data.  You will:

• Integrate cell- and tissue-resolved expression, proteomic and epigenomic datasets to delineate the regulatory subnetworks that drive pigment and specialised-metabolite production 	
• Combine these networks with the DC7 knowledge graph and explore neurosymbolic reasoning – coupling learned graph representations (graph neural networks, knowledge-graph embeddings) with symbolic rules mined from the literature graph – to infer missing pathway members and regulators with explanations a biologist can check 	
• Predict and prioritise engineering targets (regulators, enzymes, environmental cues) for experimental validation by the network’s experimental partners, and follow how those predictions fare 	
• Consolidate network- and graph-based predictions into a shared resource for the consortium   Secondment: University of Amsterdam (Prof. Ronald Koes, 3 months) to integrate transcriptomic and epigenetic datasets from petunia. You will also take part in the network’s training programme of schools, workshops and transferable-skills courses.

  Who are we looking for?  We are looking for candidates within the field(s) of bioinformatics, computational biology, computer science or data science, or plant biology with a strong quantitative interest. Experience with transcriptomics, network inference, graph machine learning or knowledge graphs is an advantage. An interest in plant metabolism is essential; a formal background in it is not.

  Our group and research – and what do we offer?  The Mutwil group at PLEN works at the interface of comparative and evolutionary plant biology and AI-driven biological discovery. We build large cross-species gene expression atlases, comparative co-expression networks and knowledge graphs, and we use machine learning and large language models to turn the plant literature and omics archives into testable hypotheses. The Department of Public Health at University of Copenhagen, Denmark, together with the The Pioneer Centre for SMARTBiomeds offers a Postdoctoral Fellowship position in causal inference with special focus on continuous-time causal inference, identification, and instrumental variables methods. 

  The anticipated hiring date is March 1, 2027, or as soon as possible hereafter.

  About the Centre

  The Pioneer Centre for Statistical and Computational Methods for Advanced Research to Transform Biomedicine (SMARTBiomed) will support a critical mass of researchers who focus on method and software development for analysis and inference from massive human data, advancing applications in medicine. The Pioneer Centre for SMARTBiomed will leverage large-scale, multimodal biomedical data combined with focused innovation in statistical and computational methods including machine learning to advance our understanding, treatment, and prevention of human disease.

  About the Section of Biostatistics
 The Section of Biostatistics carries out independent research in biostatistical applications and methods; it undertakes teaching of students at various educations, undergraduate as well as postgraduate, and it offers biostatistical advice to staff and students in all disciplines of the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences. The section is internationally renowned for a high research level, especially within time-to-event analysis, while other competence areas include e.g. causal inference, latent variable modelling and prediction models. The section aims to maintain a strong position in these areas but also wants to expand into new areas of biostatistical research. The underlying idea is to produce high-level methodological research that is relevant in practical applications.

  More information on the Section of Biostatistics can be found at: https://biostat.ku.dk/. 
  

  Job Description
 We invite highly qualified, thorough, and motivated applicants to apply for a postdoctoral position in causal inference and statistical methodology. The successful candidate will conduct methodological research at the intersection of causal inference, event-history analysis, statistical machine learning, and semiparametric theory. Research will focus on the development of statistical methods for longitudinal and time-to-event data, with particular emphasis on continuously monitored data, dynamic treatment strategies, identification, and instrumental variable methods. Potential research directions include:  

   	
• causal inference for survival and competing risks outcomes 	
• continuous-time longitudinal causal models 	
• semiparametric and machine-learning-based estimation methods 	
• identification and estimation under instrumental variable assumptions 	
• methods for treatment switching, treatment discontinuation, and dynamic treatment interventions 	
• development of efficient and robust estimators for causal effects under complex longitudinal data structures   Example projects include the development of methods for causal inference with continuously observed treatment processes, incorporation of instrumental variables into survival analysis, and machine-learning-based estimation procedures for time-varying treatment effects. The successful candidate will be expected to contribute both theoretically and computationally, including development of new methodology, investigation of statistical properties, implementation of software, simulation studies, and applications to biomedical research questions. The candidate must participate in the interdisciplinary and dynamic research environment within the Pioneer Centre for SMARTBiomed. The successful applicant is also encouraged to develop independent research directions aligned with the overall goals of the centre.

  The specific tasks of the position will include:

   	
• Manage own academic research and administrative activities. 	
• Conduct research in line with the goals of SMARTBiomed.

jobs.description:
Aalborg University Energy in Esbjerg seeks a Laboratory Engineer for a permanent, full-time position from 1 February 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. You will provide practical and technical support for research and teaching in underwater technology and help ensure that researchers and students have reliable, well-documented equipment for laboratory and field activities.

Your work tasks
You will become part of the underwater technology research environment at Aalborg University Energy in Esbjerg, where research projects combine the development, testing and application of advanced underwater robotic systems. The position provides shared technical support across several projects and contributes to coherent mechanical and electronic design practices. In this way, you will help researchers reduce duplicated technical work, strengthen knowledge sharing and reuse proven solutions across research activities.

You will work closely with researchers, students and external collaborators in a role that combines independent technical responsibility with day-to-day collaboration. Your work will take place in laboratories, workshops and field settings, depending on the activities and testing needs of the research projects. A central part of the role is to make equipment ready for use, keep it operational and support colleagues in using it safely and effectively.

You will develop laboratory and field-testing setups for underwater robotic systems, including selecting, integrating and maintaining relevant instrumentation, data acquisition equipment and data-logging systems. You will conduct laboratory and field tests involving underwater vehicles and associated sensors, support the standardisation and maintenance of electrical and mechanical hardware, and contribute to the design, development and fabrication of new components. You will also prepare user manuals and technical documentation, assist students in the operation of equipment, and help ensure that technical solutions remain accessible and reusable across projects.

Your competencies
You have a bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering, mechatronics, electronics or a related technical field. You bring practical experience with the design, development and fabrication of mechanical and electronic hardware, preferably for underwater robotic systems or comparable complex technical equipment. You are familiar with control electronics, instrumentation, data acquisition and data-logging systems, and you can use computer-aided design tools to develop and document mechanical solutions.

You have experience with robotic testing equipment and understand the importance of reliable instrumentation, systematic test procedures and clear technical documentation. Experience with the Robot Operating System or a comparable robotics framework, as well as MATLAB for data processing and analysis, is required. You communicate confidently in spoken and written English, as this is the working language in the research environment.

You work systematically and pay close attention to safety, technical quality and the practical usability of equipment. You approach technical challenges in a structured and solution-oriented way and are comfortable taking responsibility for tasks independently. jobs.description:
At AAU Energy, a position as PhD stipend is available within the general study program. The stipend is open for appointment from 1st of March 2027 or soon hereafter. The duration of the position is three years.

Your work tasks
You will develop and investigate non-aqueous liquid electrolytes for rechargeable calcium batteries, focusing on how Ca2+ solvation, ion pairing and interphase formation govern electrochemical reversibility. Your work will contribute to a complementary research programme on calcium-battery electrode materials and cell development at AAU Energy.

You will systematically vary salt chemistry, solvent composition and concentration within selected electrolyte families. Physicochemical measurements and spectroscopic analysis will be used to examine electrolyte coordination environments and ion association. These investigations will guide the selection of formulations for detailed electrochemical and interfacial studies.

A central part of the work will be the design and evaluation of calcium plating and stripping experiments, including measurements of coulombic efficiency, polarization and cycling stability under defined conditions. You will use appropriate controls and complementary analyses to verify metallic calcium deposition and distinguish it from electrolyte decomposition or other electrochemical reactions. You will investigate electrode interphase composition and evolution using XPS, supported by electron microscopy and, where appropriate, ToF-SIMS for morphology and species distribution. Raman spectroscopy, complemented by NMR where relevant, will probe electrolyte coordination and ion association. Targeted MD simulations may clarify Ca²⁺ solvation and ion pairing. Correlating these findings with electrochemical performance will establish mechanism-based guidelines for electrolyte formulation and selection.

Working closely with the PhD researcher developing cathode and calcium-alloying anode materials, you will assess selected electrode–electrolyte combinations and contribute to reproducible coin-cell evaluation. You will also contribute to scientific publications, conference presentations, teaching, supervision of student projects and departmental dissemination activities.

The position is offered in relation to the Batteries research group, and the PhD Student will be positioned to the section for “Power Electronics Systems Integration and Materials”.

jobs.description:
Your impact begins here

As Project Director, you will lead the most complex sourcing projects in Drug Substance, from category strategy through to signed contracts with CMOs, where commitments can exceed DKK 1 billion. You will shape strategies for areas of growing importance to Novo, such as synthetic peptides, and negotiate partnerships that are strong commercially and sustainable over time. Your work helps keep the supply of treatments for people living with serious chronic diseases reliable.

What you’ll bring

You are a senior sourcing and project leader who combines a strategic mindset with an eye for contractual detail.

**You Have

**

• A university master’s degree in pharmacy, biology, engineering, supply chain management, law or business.

• Around 15+ years of relevant pharmaceutical experience, in manufacturing, manufacturing development and/or CMO environments. The role may suit candidates with around 20 years of experience.

• A strong background in strategic sourcing, contract negotiation and external partner management.

• Solid experience leading complex, cross-functional projects, as project and/or line manager.

• In-depth knowledge of pharmaceutical manufacturing, CMOs, quality and regulatory requirements.

• Excellent negotiation and contracting skills, and the ability to engage with senior management and CMO executives, up to CEO level.

• The ability to lead and influence without formal authority, with resilience, autonomy, a sense of urgency and strong execution skills.

• Excellent written and spoken English.

**Useful, But Not Essential

**

• Supplementary training in areas such as cGMP, project execution or personal development.

• An existing network within Novo, CMOs and pharmaceutical engineering companies.

• Experience in Drug Product sourcing.

What you’ll do

You will own sourcing projects from the first idea to final implementation, and you will keep strategy, contract and delivery pointing in the same direction.

**In Practice, You Will

**

• Develop category strategies for areas of strategic importance, such as synthetic peptides, by pairing market insight, including global players and trends, with Novo’s strategic outlook.

• Lead critical CMO negotiations independently until signature, securing outcomes within mandate that balance value, cost, flexibility, speed and risk.

• Drive projects end-to-end: set up governance and Steering Committees, build business cases and plans, define deliverables and manage risk.

• Bring together specialists from MSAT, Supply Chain, Quality, Regulatory, Finance and Legal, and raise bottlenecks early so work keeps moving.

• Keep SVP and EVP-level stakeholders informed and aligned on progress, and give input to business plans and budgets.

• Raise the standard for how Drug Substance Outsourcing works by sharing your approach with category managers and developing sourcing standards.

Who you’ll work with

You will be a senior individual contributor in GSOD Drug Substance Outsourcing, reporting to the Senior Director of the department. You will be trusted to take decisions independently and to give strategic guidance to senior leaders on the project portfolio. You will build new skills through cross-functional and cross-border work, and you will be recognised for results through clear performance expectations.

Start now
